item.description:
What's new in 1.2.0

  • Setup now finishes what it starts. If macOS doesn't show a dialog for a permission — because it was denied once before, or the entry belongs to an older version of Cueshot — setup opens System Settings at the right place instead of quietly stopping. That was why the microphone had to be found by hand.
  • The speech model is part of setup. One download, with a progress bar, and it keeps running while you connect your coding agent. Before, you only found out it was missing the moment you wanted to dictate.
  • A granted screen recording permission is tried, not believed. macOS doesn't hand a fresh permission to an app that is already running, so setup checks whether recording actually works and asks for a restart when it doesn't — instead of showing a green checkmark and a black picture.
  • When a screen recording is refused although the permission is there, Cueshot says the real reason and offers to restart, instead of sending you to a switch you just flipped.
  • Setup picks up where it left off after a restart, rather than starting at the welcome screen again.
  • The last step says why nothing arrives when nothing arrives: input monitoring still missing, a restart still pending, or another app listening to the same double-tap.
  • The menu reports a missing speech model the same way it reports a missing permission.
